options: All of the aggregated ports use the same MAC address.
Port aggregation can be a fault tolerance mechanism.
explanation: Load balancing refers to the distribution of traffic between two or more channels. Port aggregation combines ports into a single logical channel with a single media access control (MAC) address and provides greater throughput. Port aggregation also provides fault tolerance in the event of a port failure.
whyWrong: This statement is true, because the aggregated ports act as one logical channel with one MAC address.
This statement is true, because traffic continues over the other ports when one port fails.
This statement is true, because the combined ports carry more traffic than one port.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 76
note: Book answer looks debatable: link aggregation (LACP) distributes traffic across the member links, which many sources call load balancing.

stem: Ralph is designing a new network in which the switches are connected to each other with redundant links. This redundancy enables every node on the network to communicate with any other node, even if one of the switches should fail. Which of the following is a potential drawback of this arrangement?
explanation: This redundant switch arrangement can result in broadcast storms, which are caused by packets being read by multiple switches as originating on different networks. The result is endless circulation of packets from switch to switch. The Spanning Tree Protocol prevents this by blocking the redundant links until they are needed.
whyWrong: Runt frames are frames below the minimum size, usually from collisions or faulty NICs, not from redundant links.
Late collisions come from cable segments that are too long, not from redundant switch links.
Redundant links make the lookup tables change often, but the main drawback named here is endless circulating broadcast traffic.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 77

stem: Which of the following statements about a switch's default VLAN are true?
options: Administrators must create a default VLAN when configuring a new switch.
The default VLAN on a switch cannot be deleted.
The default VLAN on most switches is designated as VLAN 0.
The default VLAN on a switch cannot be renamed.
explanation: The default VLAN in the VLAN database on most switches has the ID VLAN 1, not VLAN 0, and it cannot be deleted or renamed. The default VLAN does not have to be created by the administrator; it is the one to which all ports are assigned in the default configuration.
whyWrong: The switch creates the default VLAN itself, and every port is in it by default.
The default VLAN on most switches is VLAN 1, not VLAN 0.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 79

stem: Which of the following is the maximum transmission unit (MTU) size for an Ethernet frame?
explanation: The MTU is the largest amount of data (in bytes) that a protocol operating at a given layer of the OSI model can transmit in one packet. The MTU does not include any header and footer fields supplied by that protocol. For Ethernet, the maximum frame size is 1,518 bytes, which includes 18 bytes of header and footer fields. Therefore, the MTU for Ethernet is 1,500 bytes. Protocols operating at other OSI model layers can have different MTUs. For example, the typical MTU for an Internet Protocol (IPv4) implementation is smaller than that of Ethernet.
whyWrong: 512 bits is the minimum Ethernet frame size (64 bytes), not the MTU.
1,024 bytes is not an Ethernet limit and is smaller than the Ethernet MTU.
1,518 bytes is the maximum frame size including the 18 bytes of header and trailer, not the MTU.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 81

stem: Which of the following protocols uses jumbo frames to increase performance levels on storage area networks?
explanation: Ethernet uses jumbo frames to transfer large amounts of data more efficiently. On a packet-switched network, each packet requires header data, which adds to the network's transmission overhead. Splitting large files into a great many small packets can lead to so much overhead that network efficiency is impaired. Ethernet typically restricts frame size to 1,500 bytes, but jumbo frames enable Ethernet systems to create frames up to 9,000 bytes. Frames are Data link layer protocol data units, so Internet Protocol (IP), operating at the Network layer, is not involved in creating them. Fibre Channel and iSCSI are specialized storage area networking protocols that do not use jumbo frames.
whyWrong: IP works at the Network layer with packets, while jumbo frames are Data link layer frames.
Fibre Channel is a separate storage networking protocol with its own frame format, not Ethernet jumbo frames.
iSCSI runs over TCP/IP and benefits from jumbo frames, but the frames themselves are created by Ethernet.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 83
note: The book's explanation says iSCSI does not use jumbo frames; in practice iSCSI over Ethernet often runs with jumbo frames. The answer (Ethernet) is still correct.

stem: Which of the following topologies enables wireless devices to access resources on a wired network?
explanation: An infrastructure topology uses a wireless access point (WAP) to connect wireless devices to a wired network. An ad hoc topology connects wireless devices to each other, without connecting to a wired network. A mesh topology calls for complete interconnection of wireless nodes, which need not provide access to wired resources. The star/hub and spoke and bus topologies do not support wireless devices.
whyWrong: An ad hoc network connects wireless devices directly to each other without a link to the wired network.
Star/hub and spoke is a wired topology and does not by itself connect wireless devices to the network.
A bus is a wired topology in which devices share one cable, so it does not support wireless devices.
A mesh connects wireless nodes to each other and does not need to provide access to wired resources.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 85

stem: Which of the following components is required for two computers to communicate using an IEEE 802.11 wireless LAN in an ad hoc topology?
options: A router connected to the Internet
explanation: An ad hoc topology describes wireless computers that communicate directly with each other, without the need for any hardware other than their wireless network adapters. Therefore, the ad hoc topology does not require a router, an Internet connection, an access point (AP), or a special antenna.
whyWrong: An ad hoc network does not need a router or an Internet connection for two computers to communicate.
An ad hoc network connects the computers directly, without a wireless access point.
The built-in antennas of the wireless adapters are enough, so no external antenna is needed.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 86

stem: When designing a wireless LAN installation, which of the following are valid reasons to install a unidirectional antenna in an access point (AP), rather than an omnidirectional one? (Choose all that apply.)
options: The AP will be located against an outside wall.
There are many interior walls between the AP and the most distant workstation.
A unidirectional antenna can be focused to a specific signal pattern width.
explanation: By placing a unidirectional antenna against an outside wall, you can limit network access to users inside the structure. Unidirectional antennas provide greater signal strength than omnidirectional antennas, enabling their signals to penetrate more interior walls. It is possible to focus a unidirectional antenna to a wider or narrower signal pattern.
whyWrong: This is a valid reason, but it is only one of the listed reasons, so it is not the complete answer.
This is a valid reason, but it is only one of the listed reasons, so it is not the complete answer.
This is a valid reason, but it is only one of the listed reasons, so it is not the complete answer.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 90

stem: Which of the following are possible reasons why the 5 GHz frequency tends to perform better than the 2.4 GHz frequency on a wireless LAN? (Choose all that apply.)
options: The 5 GHz frequency has more channels than the 2.4 GHz frequency.
The 5 GHz frequency supports longer ranges than the 2.4 GHz frequency.
The 5 GHz frequency conflicts with fewer common household devices than the 2.4 GHz frequency.
The 5 GHz frequency transmits at faster speeds than the 2.4 GHz frequency.
explanation: The 5 GHz frequency has 23 channels available in the United States, while the 2.4 GHz frequency has only 11. Many household devices, such as cordless telephones, use the 2.4 GHz frequency band, but relatively few devices use the 5 GHz band. Higher frequencies typically support faster transmission speeds, because with all other conditions equal, they can carry more data in the same amount of time. The 5 GHz frequency typically has a shorter range than 2.4 GHz, because it is less able to penetrate barriers.
whyWrong: The 5 GHz band has a shorter range than 2.4 GHz because it penetrates walls and other barriers less well.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 92

stem: Alice is attempting to deploy an IEEE 802.11b/g wireless LAN on the fifth floor of a 10-story office building that is surrounded on all sides by other office buildings, all of which seem to be running many wireless LANs. Scanning the 2.4 GHz band, she sees literally dozens of networks, spread across all of the available channels. As a result, her wireless devices have trouble connecting to their access point (AP), and when they do, they achieve only low speeds. Which of the following tasks should Alice perform to enable the wireless clients to connect to the network more reliably? (Choose two.)
options: Upgrade all of the wireless network devices to IEEE 802.11n.
Configure all of the network devices to use WPA2 encryption with AES.
Configure the wireless devices to use the 5 GHz band.
Configure the AP to suppress service set identifier (SSID) broadcasts.
Upgrade all of the network devices to the latest firmware.
explanation: Upgrading the devices to 802.11n will enable them to use the 5 GHz band and evade the traffic generated by the surrounding networks. Configuring the devices to use the 5 GHz band will provide many more channels to choose from and will avoid the interference from the surrounding 2.4 GHz networks. The type of encryption that a wireless network uses has no bearing on the ability of the devices to avoid the interference generated by surrounding networks. Suppressing SSID broadcasts will not help the devices to connect to the network. Upgrading the firmware on the devices is not likely to have any effect on the connection problems when they are the result of interference from other networks.
whyWrong: The type of encryption does not help the devices avoid interference from the surrounding networks.
Hiding the SSID does not reduce interference and does not help clients connect.
New firmware will not fix connection problems caused by interference from other networks.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 93

stem: On an IEEE 802.11b/g/n wireless network running at 2.4 GHz with multiple access points (APs), the traditional best practice is to use channels 1, 6, and 11, with no two adjacent APs configured to use the same channel. Which of the following is the real reason why this is a good plan?
options: Channels 1, 6, and 11 are the only channels with frequencies that do not overlap.
Channels 1, 6, and 11 have more bandwidth than the other channels.
Channels 1, 6, and 11 have greater ranges than the other channels.
Channels 1, 6, and 11 are the default settings on most wireless devices.
explanation: Wireless LAN regulations call for 22 MHz channels in the 2.4 GHz band that are spaced 5 MHz apart, which means that they overlap. Channels 1, 6, and 11 are the only three channels that are distant enough from each other not to overlap. Therefore, they do not interfere with each other. Channels 1, 6, and 11 do not differ from the other channels in their bandwidth or their transmission range. Each wireless device can be set to use only one channel. Therefore, channels 1, 6, and 11 cannot all be the default setting.
whyWrong: All 2.4 GHz channels have the same width, so channels 1, 6, and 11 do not have more bandwidth.
All 2.4 GHz channels have about the same range, so channels 1, 6, and 11 do not reach farther.
A device can use only one channel at a time, so these three channels cannot all be the default.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 95

stem: What is the maximum channel width possible using wireless networking equipment based on the ratified IEEE 802.11 regulatory standards?
explanation: Using a technique called channel bonding, the 802.11ax and 802.11ac standards define the combination of up to eight 20 MHz channels, for a total possible channel width of 160 MHz, in a single 160 MHz channel or a non-contiguous 80+80 configuration. The 802.11n standard can bond up to two channels, for a 40 MHz width. Earlier standards are limited to a single 20 MHz channel.
whyWrong: 20 MHz is the width of one standard channel, which 802.11n and later can bond into wider channels.
40 MHz is the widest channel of 802.11n, but 802.11ac and 802.11ax can go wider.
80 MHz is not the maximum, because 802.11ac and 802.11ax can bond channels up to 160 MHz.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 97
note: Book answer reflects 802.11ac/ax; the newer IEEE 802.11be (Wi-Fi 7) standard allows 320 MHz channels.

stem: Which of the following IEEE 802.11 wireless LAN standards is capable of supporting the 6 GHz frequency band?
explanation: Only the 802.11ax standard defines wireless LAN devices that can support the 6 GHz frequency band. The 802.11a and 802.11ac standards use only 5 GHz, and the 802.11b and 802.11g standards use only 2.4 GHz. The 802.11n standard supports both the 2.4 and 5 GHz bands.
whyWrong: IEEE 802.11a uses only the 5 GHz band.
IEEE 802.11b uses only the 2.4 GHz band.
IEEE 802.11g uses only the 2.4 GHz band.
IEEE 802.11n uses the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands, not 6 GHz.
IEEE 802.11ac uses only the 5 GHz band.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 99

stem: Which of the following is the term for the network name that you use to connect a client device to an access point (AP) on a wireless LAN?
explanation: The service set identifier (SSID) is the name that you use when connecting to a wireless network. A basic service set (BSS) refers to the wireless network itself, consisting of a single AP and a number of clients. An extended service set (ESS) consists of two or more BSSs, using multiple APs. The basic service set identifier (BSSID) is the MAC address of the access point associated with a BSS. The extended service set identifier (ESSID) specifies the name of a network using multiple APs to support a single SSID.
whyWrong: A BSS is the wireless network of one AP and its clients, not the network name.
An ESS is a group of BSSs that use multiple APs, not the network name.
The BSSID is the MAC address of the access point, not the network name.
The ESSID is the name of a network that uses several APs for one SSID, not the general term for the network name.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 103

stem: Which of the following IEEE wireless LAN standards define devices with a maximum aggregate channel width of 20 MHz? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: Devices conforming to the IEEE 802.11a and 802.11g standards can only use a single 20 MHz channel. IEEE 802.11n devices can use channel bonding to join two channels together and achieve an aggregate channel width of 40 MHz. IEEE 802.11ax and 802.11ac devices can bond up to eight channels, for an aggregate width of 160 MHz, in a single channel or a non-contiguous 80+80 configuration.
whyWrong: IEEE 802.11n can bond two channels for an aggregate width of 40 MHz.
IEEE 802.11ac can bond channels for an aggregate width of up to 160 MHz.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 104

stem: Which of the following wireless security protocols provides the greatest degree of network device hardening?
explanation: Wi-Fi Protected Access 3 (WPA3) is the most secure of the wireless protocols, providing the greatest degree of network device hardening. Wi-Fi Protected Access (WPA) was created to replace the insecure Wired Equivalent Privacy (WEP) protocol, and Wi-Fi Protected Access 2 (WPA2) was created to replace the Temporal Key Integrity Protocol (TKIP) used in the first version of WPA with Advanced Encryption Standard (AES). Extensible Authentication Protocol (EAP) is a framework for the encapsulation of authentication messages.
whyWrong: WEP is the oldest and weakest wireless security protocol and is easily cracked.
WPA replaced WEP but uses TKIP, which is now also vulnerable.
WPA2 is strong but has been superseded by WPA3.
EAP is an authentication framework, not a wireless security protocol that protects the whole network.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 106

stem: Which of the following encryption protocols was introduced in the Wi-Fi Protected Access (WPA) wireless security standard?
explanation: WPA was created to replace the insecure Wired Equivalent Privacy (WEP) protocol and used Temporal Key Integrity Protocol (TKIP) with the RC4 cipher for encryption. Counter Mode with Cipher Block Chaining Message Authentication Code Protocol (CCMP) with Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) is an encryption protocol that is used with the Wi-Fi Protected Access 2 (WPA2) security protocol. Extensible Authentication Protocol (EAP) is a framework for the encapsulation of authentication messages. EAP is used on wireless networks and point-to-point connections and supports dozens of different authentication methods, including Transport Layer Security (TLS). It is not the encryption protocol used with WPA. Terminal Access Controller Access Control System Plus (TACACS+) is a protocol designed to provide AAA services for networks with many routers and switches.
whyWrong: CCMP-AES was introduced with WPA2, not the first version of WPA.
EAP-TLS is an authentication method, not the encryption protocol of WPA.
TACACS+ is an AAA protocol for network devices, not a wireless encryption protocol.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 107

stem: TKIP-RC4 is an encryption protocol used with which of the following wireless network security standards?
explanation: Wi-Fi Protected Access (WPA) was created to replace the insecure Wired Equivalent Privacy (WEP) protocol and used the Temporal Key Integrity Protocol (TKIP) with the RC4 cipher. WPA was replaced by WPA2 and later WPA3, both of which use Counter Mode with Cipher Block Chaining Message Authentication Code Protocol (CCMP) with Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) for encryption. Extensible Authentication Protocol (EAP) is a framework for the encapsulation of authentication messages.
whyWrong: WEP uses plain RC4 with static keys, not TKIP.
WPA2 replaced TKIP with CCMP-AES.
WPA3 uses CCMP-AES or stronger, not TKIP.
EAP is an authentication framework, not a security standard that uses TKIP.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 108

stem: Which of the following protocols provides wireless networks with the strongest encryption?
explanation: Wi-Fi Protected Access (WPA) is a wireless security protocol that was designed to replace the increasingly vulnerable Wired Equivalent Privacy (WEP). WPA added an encryption protocol called Temporal Key Integrity Protocol (TKIP). This too became vulnerable, and WPA2 was introduced, which replaced TKIP with the stronger CCMP-Advanced Encryption Standard (CCMP-AES). Extensible Authentication Protocol and 802.1X do not provide encryption.
whyWrong: TKIP was added to WPA as a stopgap and is now vulnerable, so it is weaker than AES.
EAP is an authentication framework and does not provide encryption.
IEEE 802.1X is a port-based access control standard and does not provide encryption.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 109

stem: To connect a wireless client to a wireless access point (WAP) using the Wi-Fi Protected Access 3-Personal (WPA3-Personal) security protocol, which of the following must you supply on both devices?
explanation: The WPA3 protocol replaces the pre-shared key of WPA2 with a Simultaneous Authentication of Equals (SAE) exchange that provides better security. SAE still requires the client and the access point (AP) to be configured with the same passphrase. The base key, the serial number, and the MAC address are all components that WPA3 uses to generate the encryption key for each packet.
whyWrong: There is no base key that the user enters on both devices.
The serial number of a device is not entered to join a WPA3-Personal network.
MAC addresses are not entered on both devices to join a WPA3-Personal network.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 110

stem: Upgrading a wireless network to the WPA3-Personal security protocol provides clients with additional protection from replay attacks. Which of the following WPA3 elements accomplish this? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: A replay attack is one in which an attacker utilizes the encryption key found in a previously captured packet to gain access to the network. Simultaneous Authentication of Equals (SAE) prevents replay attacks by including a mutual authentication process, as well as correlation of a shared passphrase. Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) prevents replay attacks by issuing a unique key for every session, so that data illicitly retained from previous sessions is rendered unusable. Pre-shared key (PSK) is the passphrase mechanism from WPA2 that has been replaced by SAE in WPA3. Near field communication (NFC) is a contact-based short-range authentication method used by some wireless implementations. Neither prevents replay attacks.
whyWrong: PSK is the WPA2 passphrase method that WPA3 replaces with SAE, and it does not stop replay attacks.
NFC is a short-range contact method used by some devices and does not stop replay attacks.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 111

stem: Which of the following wireless security protocols use CCMP-AES for encryption? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: Wi-Fi Protected Access (WPA) is a wireless security protocol that was designed to replace the increasingly vulnerable Wired Equivalent Privacy (WEP). WPA added an encryption protocol called Temporal Key Integrity Protocol (TKIP). This too became vulnerable, and WPA2 and later WPA3 were introduced, both of which replace TKIP with CCMP-Advanced Encryption Standard (CCMP-AES) encryption.
whyWrong: WEP uses RC4 with static keys, not CCMP-AES.
WPA uses TKIP with RC4, not CCMP-AES.
TKIP is itself an encryption protocol and was replaced by CCMP-AES.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 112

stem: Which of the following wireless LAN security protocols does not support the use of a pre-shared key (PSK) in its Personal configuration?
explanation: WPA3-Personal addresses WPA2's KRACK vulnerability with a more secure cryptographic handshake, replacing the PSK four-way handshake with Simultaneous Authentication of Equals (SAE), a version of the Internet Engineering Task Force's dragonfly handshake in which either client or AP can initiate contact. Each device then transmits its authentication credentials in a discrete, one-off message, instead of in a give-and-take, multipart conversation. Importantly, SAE also eliminates the reuse of encryption keys, requiring a new code with every interaction. Without open-ended communication between AP and client or encryption key reuse, cybercriminals can't as easily eavesdrop or insert themselves into an exchange. Wired Equivalent Privacy (WEP), Wi-Fi Protected Access (WPA), and Wi-Fi Protected Access 2 (WPA2) all support the use of a pre-shared key.
whyWrong: WEP supports a shared key that is entered on every device.
WPA-Personal uses a pre-shared key, which is why it is also called WPA-PSK.
WPA2-Personal uses a pre-shared key with a four-way handshake.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 113

stem: Which of the following did the Wi-Fi Protected Access 2 (WPA2) security protocol add to the existing WPA standard?
explanation: WPA2 adds Counter Mode with Cipher Block Chaining Message Authentication Code Protocol - Advanced Encryption Standard (CCMP-AES), a new symmetric key encryption algorithm that strengthens the protocol's security. Multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) is a multiplexing technology added to the IEEE 802.11n standard, not to WPA2. Wired Equivalent Protocol (WEP) is the predecessor to WPA; it is not part of WPA2. Temporal Key Integrity Protocol (TKIP) is the encryption algorithm used in the first version of WPA; it was not added in the second version.
whyWrong: MIMO is a multi-antenna technology from IEEE 802.11n, not part of WPA2.
WEP is the older protocol that WPA replaced, so WPA2 did not add it.
TKIP was already part of the first version of WPA, so WPA2 did not add it.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 114

stem: Alice is setting up a wireless LAN in a friend's home, using an 802.11n wireless access point and three computers with 802.11n adapters. She has installed and successfully tested the devices on an open network, and now she is ready to add security. Which of the following protocols should Alice choose to provide maximum security for the wireless network?
explanation: Of the options listed, Wi-Fi Protected Access 3 (WPA3) will provide the maximum security for the wireless network, in part because it uses long encryption keys that change frequently. IPsec is a Network layer security standard that does not provide the security needed for IEEE 802.11 wireless networks. Transport Layer Security (TLS) is a protocol that encrypts data exchanged by web servers and clients at the Application layer; it does not provide adequate security for wireless LANs. Layer 2 Tunneling Protocol (L2TP) is a virtual private networking protocol; it does not provide adequate security for wireless networks.
whyWrong: IPsec secures traffic at the Network layer, mainly for VPNs, and does not secure the wireless link itself.
TLS encrypts web and application sessions and does not secure the wireless link itself.
L2TP is a VPN tunneling protocol and does not secure the wireless link itself.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 115

stem: CCMP-AES is an encryption protocol used with which of the following wireless network security standards? (Choose two.)
explanation: Counter Mode with Cipher Block Chaining Message Authentication Code Protocol (CCMP) with Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) is an encryption protocol that is used with the Wi-Fi Protected Access 2 (WPA2) and Wi-Fi Protected Access 3 (WPA3) security protocols. WPA was created to replace the insecure Wired Equivalent Privacy (WEP) protocol, and WPA2 was created to replace the Temporal Key Integrity Protocol (TKIP) used in the first version of WPA. Extensible Authentication Protocol (EAP) is a framework for the encapsulation of authentication messages.
whyWrong: WEP uses RC4 with static keys, not CCMP-AES.
WPA uses TKIP with RC4, not CCMP-AES.
EAP is an authentication framework, not a security standard that uses CCMP-AES.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 116

stem: Which of the following wireless security protocols can enable network users to authenticate using smart cards?
explanation: Wi-Fi Protected Access 3 (WPA3) and Wi-Fi Protected Access 2 (WPA2) are both wireless security protocols that control access to the network and provide encryption, using protocols like Counter Mode with Cipher Block Chaining Message Authentication Code Protocol (CCMP) with Advanced Encryption Standard (AES). These protocols do not provide authentication services, however. Extensible Authentication Protocol (EAP) is a framework for the encapsulation of authentication messages. Its many variants provide support for the use of smart cards and other authentication factors, such as biometrics, in addition to traditional passwords.
whyWrong: WPA3 controls access and encrypts traffic but relies on another protocol, such as EAP, for smart card authentication.
WPA2 controls access and encrypts traffic but relies on another protocol, such as EAP, for smart card authentication.
AES is an encryption algorithm and does not authenticate users.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 117

stem: Which of the following forms of the Wi-Fi Protected Access (WPA), WPA2, and WPA3 protocols require a RADIUS server? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: WPA-Enterprise, also known as WPA-802.1X, can use the Extensible Authentication Protocol (EAP) to support various types of authentication factors and requires a Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service (RADIUS) server. WPA-Personal, also known as WPA-PSK (Pre-Shared Key), is intended for small networks and does not require RADIUS.
whyWrong: WPA-Personal uses a shared passphrase and does not need a RADIUS server.
WPA-PSK is another name for WPA-Personal, which does not need a RADIUS server.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 118

stem: Which of the following forms of the Wi-Fi Protected Access (WPA), WPA2, and WPA3 protocols call for the use of a pre-shared key (PSK)?
explanation: WPA-Personal, also known as WPA-PSK, is intended for small networks and requires a PSK. WPA-Enterprise, also known as WPA-802.1X, uses the Extensible Authentication Protocol (EAP) to support various types of authentication factors and requires a Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service (RADIUS) server.
whyWrong: WPA-Enterprise uses 802.1X and a RADIUS server instead of a pre-shared key.
WPA-EAP is another name for the Enterprise mode, which authenticates each user through EAP.
WPA-802.1X is the Enterprise mode, which uses a RADIUS server rather than a shared key.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 119

stem: Which of the following stream ciphers does the Temporal Key Integrity Protocol (TKIP) use for encryption on a wireless network?
explanation: TKIP uses the RC4 stream cipher for its encryption. Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) is used with CCMP on versions 2 and 3 of the Wi-Fi Protected Access (WPA2 and WPA3) security protocol, not version 1 (WPA), which uses TKIP. Secure Hash Algorithm (SHA) is a file hashing algorithm, not used for wireless network encryption.
whyWrong: AES is the block cipher used with CCMP in WPA2 and WPA3, not with TKIP.
CCMP is the encryption protocol that replaced TKIP, not a cipher used by it.
SHA is a hashing algorithm, not a stream cipher for wireless encryption.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 120

stem: Which of the following wireless security protocols uses CCMP for encryption?
explanation: CCMP (Counter Mode with Cipher Block Chaining Message Authentication Code Protocol) is based on the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) and is the encryption protocol used with the Wi-Fi Protected Access 2 (WPA2) and Wi-Fi Protected Access 3 (WPA3) security protocols on wireless networks. CCMP is not used with version 1 of the WPA protocol. 802.1X is an authentication protocol and is not used for encryption.
whyWrong: The first version of WPA uses TKIP with RC4, not CCMP.
802.1X is a port-based authentication standard and does not encrypt traffic.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 121

stem: CCMP is based on which of the following encryption standards?
explanation: CCMP (Counter Mode with Cipher Block Chaining Message Authentication Code Protocol) is based on the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) and is the encryption protocol used with the Wi-Fi Protected Access 2 and 3 (WPA2 and 3) security protocols on wireless networks. CCMP is not based on the Temporal Key Integrity Protocol (TKIP), which uses RC4 as its stream cipher. 802.1X is an authentication protocol and is not used for encryption.
whyWrong: TKIP is the older WPA encryption protocol that CCMP replaced.
RC4 is the stream cipher used by WEP and TKIP, not by CCMP.
802.1X is an authentication standard, not an encryption standard.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 122

stem: Ralph has installed a new wireless access point (WAP) on his network and configured it to use WPA3 for security and an SSID that is not broadcast. Which of the following describes what Ralph must do to configure his wireless clients?
options: Select the SSID from a list and allow the client to automatically detect the security protocol.
Select the SSID from a list and then select WPA3 from the security protocol options provided.
Type the SSID manually and allow the client to automatically detect the security protocol.
Type the SSID manually and then select WPA3 from the security protocol options provided.
explanation: An SSID that is not broadcast is not detectable by clients, so Ralph must type it in manually. Security protocols are also not detectable, so Ralph must configure the clients to use the same protocol he selected on the WAP.
whyWrong: A hidden SSID does not appear in the client's list of networks, so it cannot be selected there.
A hidden SSID does not appear in the list of available networks, so it must be typed in.
Clients cannot detect the security protocol of a hidden network, so it must be selected manually.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 123

stem: Which of the following encryption protocols was introduced in the Wi-Fi Protected Access 2 (WPA2) wireless security standard?
explanation: Counter Mode with Cipher Block Chaining Message Authentication Code Protocol (CCMP) with Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) is an encryption protocol that is used with the Wi-Fi Protected Access 2 (WPA2) security protocol, as well as the Wi-Fi Protected Access 3 (WPA3) protocol that followed it. WPA was created to replace the insecure Wired Equivalent Privacy (WEP) protocol, and WPA2 was created to replace the Temporal Key Integrity Protocol (TKIP) used in the first version of WPA. Extensible Authentication Protocol (EAP) is a framework for the encapsulation of authentication messages. EAP is used on wireless networks and point-to-point connections and supports dozens of different authentication methods, including Transport Layer Security (TLS). It is not the encryption protocol used with WPA2. Terminal Access Controller Access Control System Plus (TACACS+) is a protocol designed to provide AAA services for networks with many routers and switches.
whyWrong: TKIP with RC4 was the encryption used by the first version of WPA.
EAP-TLS is an authentication method, not the encryption protocol of WPA2.
TACACS+ is an AAA protocol for managing network devices, not wireless encryption.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 124

stem: Which of the following wireless LAN security protocols were rendered obsolete after they were found to be extremely easy to penetrate? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: Wired Equivalent Privacy (WEP) was one of the first commercially available security protocols for wireless LANs, but it was soon found to be easily penetrated and was replaced by Wi-Fi Protected Access (WPA). WPA was also deprecated in 2015 due to multiple security weaknesses, leading to the introduction of Wi-Fi Protected Access 2 (WPA2) and then WPA3. Extensible Authentication Protocol (EAP) is a framework for the encapsulation of authentication messages.
whyWrong: WPA2 with CCMP-AES is still in use and was not deprecated as easy to penetrate.
WPA3 is the newest Wi-Fi security protocol and is not obsolete.
EAP is an authentication framework, not a wireless LAN security protocol that was retired.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 125

stem: Which of the following encryption ciphers was replaced by CCMP-AES when the WPA2 wireless security protocol was introduced?
explanation: WPA2 was introduced when the earlier version of Wi-Fi Protected Access (WPA) was determined to be increasingly vulnerable to attack. WPA used an encryption protocol called Temporal Key Integrity Protocol (TKIP). WPA2 replaced TKIP with an Advanced Encryption Standard (CCMP-AES) protocol.
whyWrong: EAP is an authentication framework and was not replaced by CCMP-AES.
WEP was replaced by WPA, which brought in TKIP before WPA2 brought in CCMP-AES.
CCMP is the protocol that did the replacing, not the one that was replaced.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 126

stem: Ralph is installing a wireless LAN that includes three access points (APs) to provide coverage for a large building. Which of the following must Ralph do to ensure that users are able to roam without interruption from one AP to another using their portable devices? (Choose all that apply.)
options: Configure each AP with the same IP address.
Configure each AP with the same security passphrase.
Configure each AP to use the same security protocol.
Configure each AP with the same SSID.
explanation: Roaming from one AP to another without interruption requires that the APs all use the same SSID, the same security protocol, and the same passphrase. The APs will not function properly if they have the same IP address.
whyWrong: Each AP needs its own unique IP address, and duplicate addresses would cause conflicts.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 127

stem: Which of the following protocols can be used by wireless controllers to communicate with the access points (APs) on a wireless local area network (WLAN)? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: The Control and Provisioning of Wireless Access Points (CAPWAP) protocol and the Lightweight Access Point Protocol (LWAPP) both enable wireless controllers to manage and control access points (APs). Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) is used by directory services, and Point-to-Point Tunneling Protocol (PPTP) is used for virtual private networking.
whyWrong: LDAP is a directory services protocol, not an access point control protocol.
PPTP is an old VPN tunneling protocol, not a wireless controller protocol.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 134

stem: On a wireless network, which of the following BEST describes an example of a captive portal?
options: A switch port used to connect to other switches
A web page with which a user must interact before being granted access to a wireless network
A series of two doors through which people must pass before they can enter a secured space
A web page stating that the user's computer has been locked and will only be unlocked after payment of a fee
explanation: A captive portal is a web page displayed to a user attempting to access a public wireless network. The user typically must supply credentials, provide payment, or accept a user agreement before access is granted. A captive portal does not refer to a switch port, a secured entryway to a room, or a type of extortionate computer attack.
whyWrong: A switch port that connects to other switches is an uplink or trunk port.
Two doors that a person must pass through form an access control vestibule.
A page that demands payment to unlock a computer is a ransomware attack.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 135

stem: A user attempting to connect to a Wi-Fi hotspot in a coffee shop is taken to a web page that requires her to accept an end-user license agreement (EULA) before access to the network is granted. Which of the following is the term for such an arrangement?
explanation: A web page that prompts users for payment, authentication, or acceptance of a EULA is a captive portal. Ransomware is a type of attack that extorts payment. Port security and root guards are methods for protecting access to switch ports.
whyWrong: Ransomware is malware that encrypts or locks data and demands payment.
Port security limits which MAC addresses can use a switch port.
Root guard is a switch feature that protects the spanning tree root bridge.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 136

stem: A wireless access point (WAP) enables computers equipped with wireless network interface adapters to function in which of the following topologies?
explanation: A WAP is a device with a wireless transceiver that also connects to a standard cabled network. Wireless computers communicate with the WAP, which forwards their transmissions over the network cable. This is called an infrastructure topology. A star/hub and spoke or bus network requires the computers to be physically connected to the network cable, and an ad hoc topology is one in which wireless computers communicate directly with one another.
whyWrong: A star/hub and spoke topology connects computers to a central device by cable.
In an ad hoc topology, wireless devices talk directly to each other without an access point.
A bus topology connects computers to one shared cable.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 137

stem: A wireless network adapter that automatically chooses the best available network frequency, 2.4 GHz or 5 GHz, based on signal strength and distance from the access point, is performing which of the following functions?
explanation: Band steering is a wireless network adapter mechanism that evaluates the available wireless signals and automatically chooses the best frequency for the current conditions. Channel bonding is a wireless networking technique that combines channels to increase bandwidth. Link aggregation is a term for technology in which the bandwidth of multiple network adapter connections is joined to speed up transmissions. Traffic shaping is a means of prioritizing network traffic by delaying packets at the Application layer.
whyWrong: Channel bonding joins adjacent channels to make a wider channel with more bandwidth.
Link aggregation joins several wired network connections into one logical link.
Traffic shaping delays some packets to give priority to other traffic.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 138

stem: Which of the following types of wireless access point (WAP) requires the network to include a wireless LAN controller (WLC)?
explanation: Lightweight wireless access points are designed to facilitate the expansion of the network by using a single wireless LAN controller (WLC) to store and deploy the configuration parameters for multiple lightweight access points configured to use the same SSID. Standalone and autonomous are terms for the same type of combined switch and access point commonly used today. There is no such thing as a traffic access point.
whyWrong: A standalone access point stores its own configuration and needs no controller.
An autonomous access point is managed on its own and needs no controller.
There is no such access point type as a traffic access point.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 139

stem: At what humidity level do electronic components become vulnerable to damage from electrostatic shock?
explanation: Humidity prevents the buildup of static electricity that can cause discharges that damage equipment. Humidity levels of 50 percent or lower can cause equipment to be susceptible to electrostatic shock. Datacenters therefore keep humidity in a controlled range, high enough to limit static and low enough to avoid condensation.
whyWrong: The book gives 50 percent as the threshold, so 30 percent is not the level where the risk starts.
Humidity above 70 percent reduces static but risks condensation and corrosion.
Humidity above 90 percent causes condensation, not static discharge.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 140

stem: Ralph is designing the HVAC implementation for his company's new central datacenter, which will house all of the equipment for the corporate headquarters and the company's manufacturing facility. The datacenter must adhere to the Tier III standard defined by the Uptime Institute, which calls for at least 99.9 percent uptime. As part of the environmental infrastructure for the datacenter, Ralph plans to install sensors to monitor environmental factors that can affect computer equipment and generate alerts when conditions exceed accepted thresholds. Which of the following environmental factors is not one of those that Ralph should arrange to monitor to protect the equipment specific to a datacenter?
explanation: Unless there is a specific known threat at the datacenter location, radon is not one of the environmental factors that typically can affect equipment uptime and that needs to be monitored. Temperature, humidity, flooding, and static electricity, however, are factors that should be monitored in a datacenter, as variations of these elements can result in equipment damage and downtime.
whyWrong: Flooding can destroy datacenter equipment, so water sensors should be monitored.
Humidity affects static buildup and condensation, so it should be monitored.
Static electricity can damage components, so it should be monitored.
Temperature affects equipment cooling and reliability, so it should be monitored.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 141

stem: Which of the following are places where network wiring connections are found? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: A large enterprise network will—at minimum—have demarcation points for telephone services and a connection to an Internet service provider's (ISP's) network. In many cases, these services will enter the building in the same equipment room that houses the backbone switch. This room is then called the main distribution frame (MDF). An intermediate distribution frame (IDF) is the location of localized telecommunications equipment such as the interface between the horizontal cabling and the backbone. Mean time between failure (MTBF) and Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) are not locations of network wiring.
whyWrong: MTBF is a reliability metric for hardware, not a wiring location.
RDP is a remote desktop protocol, not a wiring location.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 142

stem: Which of the following is the term used to describe a wiring nexus—typically housed in a closet—where horizontal networks meet the backbone?
explanation: An intermediate distribution frame (IDF) is the location of localized telecommunications equipment such as the interface between a horizontal network, which connects to workstations and other user devices, and the network backbone. A large enterprise network will typically have demarcation points for telephone services and a connection to an Internet service provider's (ISP's) network. In many cases, these services will enter the building in the same equipment room that houses the backbone switch. This room is then called the main distribution frame (MDF). Mean time between failure (MTBF), service-level agreements (SLAs), and memoranda of understanding (MOUs) are not locations of network wiring.
whyWrong: The MDF is the main equipment room where outside services and the backbone switch are found.
MTBF is a reliability metric for hardware, not a wiring location.
An SLA is a service contract, not a wiring location.
An MOU is an agreement between parties, not a wiring location.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 143

stem: Redundant power circuits can enable a server to continue running despite which of the following events?
options: A failure of the server's uninterruptable power supply (UPS)
explanation: If a server is connected to two building circuits, it can continue to function if the breaker for one circuit trips and remains uncorrected. All of the other options will bring the server down unless additional redundancies are in place. Redundant circuits protect only against the loss of one circuit inside the building.
whyWrong: A citywide outage cuts power to every building circuit, so redundant circuits do not help.
A failed server power supply needs a redundant power supply, not a redundant circuit.
If the server's single UPS fails, the server loses power unless it has another UPS.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 145

stem: A server with dual power supplies must be running in which of the following modes for the system to be fault tolerant?
explanation: A server with dual power supplies can run in one of two modes: redundant or combined. In redundant mode, both power supplies are capable of providing 100 percent of the power needed by the server. Therefore, the server can continue to run if one power supply fails, making it fault tolerant. In combined mode, both power supplies are needed to provide the server's needs, so a failure of one power supply will bring the server down. Individual mode and hot backup mode are not terms used for this purpose.
whyWrong: In combined mode both power supplies are needed, so one failure brings the server down.
Individual mode is not a term used for dual power supply operation.
Hot backup mode is not a term used for dual power supply operation.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 146

stem: Which of the following statements about the differences between online and standby uninterruptible power supplies (UPSs) are correct? (Choose all that apply.)
options: A standby UPS runs devices using battery power all the time.
An online UPS provides no gap in the power supplied to the devices during a main power failure.
An online UPS switches devices to battery power only during a main power failure.
A standby UPS provides only enough power for an orderly shutdown of the devices.
explanation: It is an online UPS that runs devices using battery power all the time so that there is no gap in the power supplied to devices during a failure. It is a standby UPS that switches devices to battery power during a main power failure. Both online and standby UPSs provide only enough power for an orderly shutdown of the devices.
whyWrong: It is the online UPS, not the standby UPS, that runs devices from the battery all the time.
It is the standby UPS that switches to battery power only when the main power fails.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 147

stem: Which of the following are valid reasons why online uninterruptible power supplies (UPSs) are more expensive than standby UPSs?
options: Online UPSs enable devices to run longer when a main power failure occurs.
Online UPSs enable devices to run continuously when a main power failure occurs.
Online UPSs are managed devices that can generate alerts.
Online UPSs provide greater protection against power spikes and sags.
explanation: Online UPSs run devices from their battery all the time, while simultaneously keeping the battery charged. There is therefore no switchover gap when a power failure occurs. Online UPSs do not necessarily run longer than standby UPSs, nor do they provide more protection against power spikes and sags. Both online and standby UPSs can be managed devices.
whyWrong: Run time depends on battery capacity, not on whether the UPS is online or standby.
Both online and standby UPSs can be managed devices that send alerts.
The book does not treat spike and sag protection as the reason for the higher price of an online UPS.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 148
note: The book's answer is kept. An online (double-conversion) UPS does condition power and gives better protection against sags and spikes than a standby UPS, so the spikes-and-sags option is arguably also correct.

stem: Which of the following is the primary function of an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) during a two-hour building power failure?
options: To keep servers running until building power is restored
To keep servers running until they can be powered down safely
To keep servers from being damaged by power spikes
To keep servers running in the event of a computer power supply failure
explanation: UPSs can provide servers with battery backup power, but usually only for a few minutes, so that the servers can be powered down safely, without the potential for data corruption or loss. UPSs typically cannot keep servers running for two hours. UPSs can protect against power spikes, but that is not their primary function. A computer power supply failure will bring a server down, regardless of the presence of a UPS.
whyWrong: Most UPS batteries last only minutes, so they cannot keep servers running for two hours.
A UPS can block power spikes, but that is not its primary function in an outage.
A UPS cannot help when the server's own power supply fails.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 149

stem: If you have a server with dual power supplies, one of which is plugged into a single uninterruptible power supply (UPS) and the other into a wall socket with a surge protector, and the building's power circuit is connected to a backup generator, which of the following failures can the server survive and keep running indefinitely? (Choose all that apply.)
options: Failure of one server power supply
Failure of the building power circuit
Failure of the building backup generator
explanation: If one of the server's power supplies fails, the other will continue to function. If the UPS fails, the server will continue to use the power supply plugged into the wall socket. If the building's backup generator fails, the server will continue to run as long as the building still has outside power. If the breaker for the building power circuit trips, the server will run only as long as the UPS battery holds out.
whyWrong: If the building circuit fails, the server runs only until the UPS battery is empty.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 150

stem: If you have a server with dual power supplies, each of which is connected to a separate uninterruptible power supply (UPS), with each UPS connected to a separate building power circuit connected to a backup generator, which of the following failures can the server survive and keep running indefinitely? (Choose all that apply.)
options: Failure of one server power supply
Failure of one building power circuit
Failure of the building backup generator
explanation: If one of the server's power supplies fails, the other will continue to function. If one of the UPSs fails, the server will continue to run using the other. If one of the building power circuit breakers trips, the server will continue to run using the other one. If the building's backup generator fails, the server will continue to run as long as the building still has outside power.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 151

stem: Which of the following is the most commonly recommended fire suppression system for a datacenter?
explanation: Clean agents are non-conductive inert gases that extinguish flame by rapid cooling and oxygen displacement without leaving any residue behind to damage equipment. Both pre-action sprinklers and water mist systems spray water, which can damage electronic equipment. Carbon dioxide is a fire suppressant, but it is also too toxic to be used on a large scale.
whyWrong: Carbon dioxide puts out fires but is too toxic for large occupied spaces.
Pre-action sprinklers still spray water, which can damage electronic equipment.
Water mist systems spray water, which can damage electronic equipment.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 152

stem: Which of the following is the primary difference between the power distribution units (PDUs) used in datacenters and the standard power strips used in offices and homes?
explanation: A PDU for a datacenter performs the same basic function as an office power strip, but it typically has a larger power input. It does not necessarily have more outlets or a larger voltage output. PDUs often take a high-amperage or three-phase feed and spread it across the equipment in a rack.
whyWrong: A datacenter PDU does not necessarily have more outlets than a power strip.
A datacenter PDU does not necessarily supply a higher output voltage.
Only the larger power input is the main difference, so not all of the options are correct.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 153

stem: Which of the following is the term used to describe a wiring nexus that is typically the termination point for incoming telephone and wide area network (WAN) services?
explanation: A large enterprise network will—at minimum—have demarcation points for telephone services and a connection to an Internet service provider's (ISP's) network. In many cases, these services will enter the building in the same equipment room that houses the backbone switch. This room is then called the main distribution frame (MDF). An intermediate distribution frame (IDF) is the location of localized telecommunications equipment such as the interface between the horizontal cabling and the backbone. Mean time between failure (MTBF), Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP), and memorandum of understanding (MOU) are not locations of network wiring.
whyWrong: MTBF is a reliability metric for hardware, not a wiring location.
An IDF connects horizontal cabling to the backbone on a floor, not the incoming WAN services.
RDP is a remote desktop protocol, not a wiring location.
An MOU is an agreement between parties, not a wiring location.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 155

stem: In an internal UTP cable installation, each horizontal cable run connects a wall plate in the work area to a centralized cabling nexus in a telecommunications room. Which of the following is the correct term for this cabling nexus?
explanation: The cabling nexus in a telecommunications room is called a patch panel. A telepole is a tool used for installing cables. A demarcation point, or demarc, is the location at which a telecommunication provider's service meets the customer's private network. A backbone is a network that connects other local area networks (LANs) together. A fiber distribution panel is used for fiber-optic cable, not unshielded twisted-pair (UTP), connections.
whyWrong: A telepole is a tool for running cables in ceilings, not a cabling nexus.
A demarc is where the provider's service meets the customer's network.
A backbone is the network that connects other LANs together.
A fiber distribution panel terminates fiber-optic cable, not UTP cable.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 175

stem: Datacenter equipment racks are typically ruled into vertical rack units, which are standard-sized divisions that hardware manufacturers use when manufacturing rack-mountable components. Which of the following is the standard vertical height of a single rack unit?
explanation: A single rack unit is 1.75 inches, or 44.5 mm. Many components that are one rack unit tall are actually 1.721 inches high, which leaves a small space between components for easy insertion and removal.
whyWrong: 1.721 inches is the actual height of many 1U devices, which leaves a small gap between them.
40 mm is less than one rack unit, which is about 44.5 mm.
3.5 inches is the height of two rack units.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 176

stem: Ralph is evaluating switches and, in the documentation for some of the switch models, he sees an option allowing the switch to be set for port-side intake or port-side exhaust. Ralph is not sure what this option does. Which of the following BEST describes the function of the port side intake/exhaust setting?
options: The setting specifies the direction that incoming signals take through the row of switch ports: left to right or right to left.
The setting specifies which set of cable ports should be active: front or back.
The setting specifies the direction of the airflow through the switch: front to back or back to front.
explanation: The port-side intake/exhaust option controls the flow of air through the switch. An administrator can specify whether the vents on the front of the switch take air in and exhaust it out the back or exhaust air taken in through the back. This enables administrators to designate specific aisles in the datacenter as warm or cold. The port-side intake/exhaust option has nothing to do with the signal propagation through the switch or which ports the switch should use.
whyWrong: The setting does not control the direction of signals across the ports.
The setting does not choose which set of ports is active.
Only the airflow description is correct, so not all of the options apply.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 177

stem: Alice is designing the datacenter for her company's new facility and is attempting to calculate the total power load for the entire datacenter. Which of the following functions should Alice include in her power load calculations? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: In addition to the actual networking equipment, such as servers, switches, and routers, the power load calculations for a datacenter must include HVAC (and particularly cooling and fire suppression), room lighting, and any other powered security equipment. The intermediate distribution frame (IDF) is not located in the datacenter and therefore does not factor in Alice's power load calculations.
whyWrong: The IDF is not located in the datacenter, so it is not part of the datacenter's power load.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 178

stem: Which of the following is a wireless topology that does not require the use of an access point?
explanation: An ad hoc topology (also known as an independent basic service set) is one in which wireless computers communicate directly with one another without the need for an access point. A wireless access point is a device with a wireless transceiver that also connects to a standard cabled network. Wireless computers communicate with the access point, which forwards their transmissions over the network cable. This is called an infrastructure topology. Star and bus topologies are not used by wireless networks; they require the computers to be physically connected to the network cable.
whyWrong: A star topology connects devices to a central device by cable.
A bus topology connects devices to one shared cable.
An infrastructure topology requires an access point that connects wireless clients to the network.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 6: Practice Test 1, Practice Test 1 question 6

stem: Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) is an encryption algorithm that was introduced in the Wi-Fi Protected Access 2 (WPA2) security protocol to replace another algorithm that was found to be easily penetrated. Which of the following encryption algorithms did AES replace?
explanation: Wi-Fi Protected Access (WPA) is the wireless security protocol that was designed to replace the increasingly vulnerable Wired Equivalent Privacy (WEP) protocol. WPA added an encryption algorithm called Temporal Key Integrity Protocol (TKIP) that was more difficult to penetrate. Over time, however, TKIP too became vulnerable, and WPA2 was introduced, which replaced TKIP with the Advanced Encryption Standard algorithm (AES).
whyWrong: AES is the algorithm that did the replacing, so it cannot have replaced itself.
WEP is a security protocol that WPA replaced, not the algorithm that AES replaced.
WPA is a security protocol, while AES replaced its TKIP encryption algorithm.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 6: Practice Test 1, Practice Test 1 question 9

stem: You are setting up an 802.11n wireless network using the 2.4 GHz frequency band. You plan to install three wireless access points. Which of the following channels should you use for your access points to avoid channel overlap that can result in interference? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: The 2.4 GHz band used by wireless LANs (WLANs) consists of channels that are 20 (or 22) MHz wide. However, the channels are only 5 MHz apart, so it is possible for channel overlap to occur between the access points, which can result in interference. Channels 1, 6, and 11 are the only channels that are far enough apart from each other to avoid any overlap with the adjacent channels. Channels 4 and 8 are susceptible to overlap.
whyWrong: Channel 4 overlaps with channels 1 and 6.
Channel 8 overlaps with channels 6 and 11.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 6: Practice Test 1, Practice Test 1 question 15

stem: You are installing an Internet access router for your company's new branch office. The router has a switch module containing four Ethernet ports, all of which are assigned to the default VLAN1. When you plug a laptop into one of the Ethernet ports, you can access the Internet with no difficulties. You now need to connect the router to the company network so that the wireless access points on the network can provide users with Internet access through the router. However, when you plug the router into a network switch port that is assigned to VLAN4, the switch starts generating “Native VLAN mismatch detected” errors once every minute. Which of the following steps should be part of the solution you implement to stop the error messages from appearing? (Choose all that apply.)
options: Create a VLAN1 on the network switch.
Configure the network switch port connected to the router to use VLAN1.
Create a VLAN4 on the router's switch module.
Configure the router port connected to the network switch to use VLAN4.
explanation: The solution requires you to create a VLAN on the ADSL router that matches the VLAN the network switch port is using. Therefore, you should create a VLAN4 on the router's switch module and assign an Ethernet port to it, which will be the port you use to connect the ADSL router to the network switch. There is no need to create a VLAN1 on the network switch, because all switches already have a default VLAN called VLAN1. Modifying the VLAN assignments on the network switch is not a good idea, because it might interfere with the existing VLAN strategy in place.
whyWrong: Every switch already has a default VLAN1, so there is no need to create one.
Changing the network switch port's VLAN could interfere with the existing VLAN plan.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 6: Practice Test 1, Practice Test 1 question 20

stem: You have constructed a network on which all of the computers are connected to a single switch. You then create virtual local area networks (VLANs) on the switch, corresponding to the company's departments, and add the switch port for each user workstation and department server to the appropriate VLAN. Later, users report that while they can access their departmental servers and the workstations of other users in the same department, they cannot communicate with any of the other departments. What is the problem, and what must you do to correct it?
options: There is a faulty VLAN configuration on the switch. You must re-create all of the VLANs and configure each VLAN for routing.

VLANs are limited to Data link layer communication only. To enable communication between the VLANs, you must install a router or a layer 3 switch on the network and configure it to route traffic between the VLANs.
The VLANs are using different Data link layer protocols. You must configure the VLANs to use the same Data link layer protocol in order for them to communicate with each other.
One of the VLANs is configured to filter all of the other VLAN traffic for security purposes. You must change the filter on this one VLAN.
explanation: VLANs are virtual layer 2 (Data link layer) LANs defined within switches. As with physical LANs, only devices in the same VLAN can communicate with each other until a layer 3 device, such as a router or a layer 3 switch, is added to the network. Re-creating and reconfiguring the VLANs will not correct the problem. Traffic filters are usually implemented on routers, not switches. Once a router is in place, VLANs do not have to use the same data link protocol to communicate with each other.
whyWrong: The VLANs work as designed, and re-creating them does not add routing between them.
The VLANs on one switch do not use different data link protocols, and that is not why they are isolated.
VLANs do not filter each other's traffic, and the switch does not have such a filter.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 6: Practice Test 1, Practice Test 1 question 28

stem: The jumbo frame capability is associated with which networking protocol?
explanation: Ethernet uses jumbo frames at the Data link layer to transfer large amounts of data more efficiently. Ethernet typically restricts frame size to 1,500 bytes, but jumbo frames enable Ethernet systems to create frames up to 9,000 bytes. PPP does not support the use of jumbo frames. Frames are protocol data units (PDUs) associated only with the Data link layer, so they do not apply to IP and TCP, which operate at the Network and Transport layers, respectively.
whyWrong: IP is a Network layer protocol that works with packets, not frames.
PPP does not support jumbo frames.
TCP is a Transport layer protocol that works with segments, not frames.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 6: Practice Test 1, Practice Test 1 question 37

stem: Which of the following are switch features that help to prevent intruders from manipulating the Spanning Tree Protocol (STP)?
explanation: BPDU guard and root guard are both mechanisms that protect the Spanning Tree Protocol against infiltration by attackers. Bridge protocol data units (BPDUs) are messages that switches running the Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) exchange to learn about the available paths through a switched network. Switches should receive BPDUs only through ports connected to other switches. BPDU guard is a feature that prevents BPDU messages from arriving through ports connected to end systems, such as computers. A root guard affects the behavior of the STP by enforcing the selection of root bridge ports on a switched network. Without root guards, there is no way for administrators to enforce the topology of a network with a redundant switching fabric. Geofencing is a wireless technology that uses radio frequency identification (RFID) or GPS coordinates to define a geographic perimeter for a network. DHCP snooping is a security feature that prevents unauthorized DHCP servers from accessing the network.
whyWrong: Geofencing defines a geographic perimeter for network access and does not protect STP.
DHCP snooping blocks unauthorized DHCP servers, not STP manipulation.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 6: Practice Test 1, Practice Test 1 question 40

stem: Network cable runs generally connect office endpoints, such as wall plates, to a central cabling nexus, which is typically where the runs are joined to a backbone network that links them together. Which of the following are terms for such nexuses where network cabling connections are found? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: A large enterprise network will—at minimum—have demarcation points for telephone services and a connection to an Internet service provider's network. In many cases, these services enter the building in the same equipment room that houses the backbone switch, which enables all the devices on the network to access those resources. This room is then called the main distribution frame (MDF). An intermediate distribution frame (IDF) is a place where localized telecommunications equipment, such as the interface between the horizontal cabling and the backbone, is located. For example, an enterprise network housed in a single building might have its MDF in the basement and an IDF on each floor. Mean time between failures (MTBF) and Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) are not network cabling locations.
whyWrong: RDP is a remote desktop protocol, not a cabling location.
MTBF is a reliability metric for hardware, not a cabling location.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 6: Practice Test 1, Practice Test 1 question 41

stem: Which of the following is not a term for the process of combining the bandwidth of two or more network adapters to increase the overall speed of the connection and provide fault tolerance?
explanation: Clustering refers to the combination of multiple servers—not network adapters—into a single unit to enhance performance and provide fault tolerance. Bonding, link aggregation, port aggregation, and NIC teaming are all terms for the same basic technology, in which the bandwidth of multiple network adapter connections is joined to speed up transmissions. The technology also enables the network communication to continue if one of the adapters fails or is disconnected.
whyWrong: Port aggregation is a term for combining network adapter connections.
Link aggregation is a term for combining network adapter connections.
Bonding is a term for combining network adapter connections.
NIC teaming is a term for combining network adapter connections.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 6: Practice Test 1, Practice Test 1 question 43

stem: Which of the following specifies the name of a network using multiple APs to support a single SSID?
explanation: On a wireless network, an extended service set identifier (ESSID) is used to identify a configuration in which there is a single SSID using multiple access points. A basic service set (BSS) refers to the wireless network itself, consisting of a single AP and a number of clients. An extended service set (ESS) consists of two or more BSSs, using multiple APs. The service set identifier (SSID) is the name that you use when connecting to a wireless network. The basic service set identifier (BSSID) is the MAC address of the access point associated with a BSS.
whyWrong: A BSS is one access point and its clients, not a name for a multi-AP network.
An ESS is the set of BSSs itself, while its identifier is the ESSID.
The SSID is the network name a client connects to, not the identifier of a multi-AP configuration.
A BSSID is the MAC address of one access point in a BSS.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 6: Practice Test 1, Practice Test 1 question 51

stem: You are designing a new wireless network based on the IEEE 802.11n standard. The equipment you have selected supports both the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz frequencies, and you are undecided about which one to use. Which of the following are possible reasons why the 5 GHz frequency tends to perform better than the 2.4 GHz frequency on a wireless LAN? (Choose all that apply.)
options: The 5 GHz frequency has more channels than the 2.4 GHz frequency.
The 5 GHz frequency conflicts with fewer common household devices than the 2.4 GHz frequency.
The 5 GHz frequency transmits at faster speeds than the 2.4 GHz frequency.
The 5 GHz frequency supports longer ranges than the 2.4 GHz frequency.
explanation: The 5 GHz frequency has 23 channels available in the United States, whereas the 2.4 GHz frequency has only 11. Many household devices, such as cordless telephones, use the 2.4 GHz frequency band, but relatively few devices use the 5 GHz band.
